purpose: Insulin glargine-aglr is used to help control blood sugar levels in adults and children with diabetes, including both type 1 and type 2 diabetes. It works all day and night to keep your blood sugar from getting too high. It is not used to treat sudden episodes of low blood sugar.
how_it_works: This insulin works just like the natural insulin your body makes, helping sugar from your blood get into your cells for energy. It is released slowly and steadily over about 24 hours, giving you around-the-clock blood sugar control. Think of it as a slow, gentle background insulin that keeps your levels stable throughout the day and night.
common_side_effects: The most common side effect is low blood sugar (hypoglycemia), which can cause shakiness, sweating, dizziness, confusion, or hunger. You may also notice redness, swelling, or itching at the injection site. Some people experience weight gain over time.
warnings: Low blood sugar is the biggest risk — always have a fast-acting sugar source nearby, like glucose tablets or juice. Never share your insulin pen or needles with anyone else, even if the needle is changed. Tell your doctor if you have kidney or liver problems, are pregnant, or are planning to become pregnant. Do not mix this insulin with other insulins in the same syringe. Alcohol and certain medicines can affect your blood sugar levels.
typical_dosing: This insulin is given as a shot under the skin (subcutaneous injection) once a day, at the same time each day. Your doctor will decide your starting dose based on your needs. The dose is usually adjusted gradually until your blood sugar is well controlled. Never change your dose without talking to your doctor or diabetes care team first.
